This project investigates global measles outbreak data using the [TidyTuesday 24-06-2025 dataset](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2025/2025-06-24), analysed on 25-06-2025. Using WHO provisional reports from 2015--2025, the analysis highlights vulnerable countries, under-reported outbreaks, and population-level immunisation challenges.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## <i class="bi bi-grid-1x2"></i>Key Features

-   <i class="bi bi-grid-3x3"></i> **Seasonal Heatmap** of monthly outbreak patterns for top countries.
-   <i class="bi bi-circle"></i> **Bubble Chart** showing vaccine coverage gaps for large populations
-   <i class="bi bi-diagram-2"></i> **Scatter Plot** to detect under-reporting by comparing incidence and totals

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## <i class="bi bi-lightbulb"></i>Key Insights

-   Seasonal patterns show distinct outbreak peaks across regions, supporting the need for region-specific vaccination timing.

-   High-incidence countries like Madagascar, Mongolia, and Kyrgyzstan had relatively low total case counts, suggesting possible under-reporting.

-   The scatter plot revealed several countries with inconsistent surveillance, highlighting a gap in global health reporting systems.

-   Countries with low vaccine coverage and large populations such as Nigeria and Pakistan are critical priorities for public health interventions.

-   The bubble chart enabled identification of outlier regions where vaccine programs may not be translating into coverage or protection, warranting further investigation.
